svg.title: Window functions compared: shape and leakage
svg.desc: Left: the rectangular, Hann, Hamming and Blackman windows across one block of samples. The rectangular window stays at 1; Hann and Blackman fall to 0 at both ends; Hamming falls to 0.08. Right: four small charts of the spectrum each window gives a single tone, in decibels, from 10 bins below to 10 bins above it. The highest side lobes are -13 dB for rectangular, -31 dB for Hann, -43 dB for Hamming and -58 dB for Blackman, while the central peak gets wider in the same order.
svg.text: Window shape (left) and the leakage it causes (right)
Weight given to each sample in the block
Spectrum of one tone, dB, by bins from the tone
Dashed line: the highest side lobe. Lower means less leakage; a wider central peak means less detail.
